clue.text: Mostly you infanticides are involved in production of cartoon-style takeover of the world

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped
letters that are involved get tangled up together and come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lurid charge that murderous children are behind a cartoon empire's global conquest.
explanation.walkthrough: YO (you without its last letter) joins INFANTICIDES, and all fourteen letters are rearranged into DISNEYFICATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the spread of a theme-park, animated-film style of sanitised culture across every country.

clue.text: Lad in panic: sir is half-crazy flogger

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word keeps just its opening letter here
crazy suggests disorder, so the letters are thrown into a different sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first half of this little word

explanation.surface: A schoolboy panics before a teacher who is half mad and fond of the cane.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon and 'sir' paint an old-fashioned school; 'is half' supplies just I to complete the fourteen letters of DISCIPLINARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enforces strict rules with harsh punishment, historically including beatings, fits this loose description.

clue.text: Mix-up rattles minor celebrity

indicators.note: a mix-up is a muddle, so the following letters are jumbled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some confusion upsets a minor public figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A young actress or performer hyped as a future star but not yet famous is a minor celebrity.

clue.text: After topless sex, writing style become digressive

indicators.note: without its top, a down entry loses its first letter
placing one piece after the other tells us the order in which they join

blocks.note: taken as written, then beheaded
joined-up handwriting is called cursive

explanation.surface: Someone's prose wanders off topic after some racy topless encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' suggests nudity, but in a down clue it just means the first letter goes. Cursive is joined-up handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that makes excursions away from its main subject wanders off the point, which is what digressive means.

clue.text: Normal Stanley makes arrows

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: one who makes arrows

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of Norman Stanley, the lag played by Ronnie Barker in the British sitcom Porridge
second meaning: a craftsman who fits arrows with feathers

explanation.walkthrough: Porridge was a 1970s British prison sitcom whose hero was Norman Stanley Fletcher; the printed 'Normal' is a misprint for Norman.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom convict bears this surname, and the same word is the old trade name for an arrow-maker.

clue.text: Offhand about sexual irregularity without former partner

indicators.note: an irregularity means things are out of their proper order, so the letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so the letters for the ex-partner are removed

blocks.note: ca, short for the Latin circa, means about
taken as written
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone is blase about straying sexually once their ex is out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: CA comes first; SEXUAL rearranged with EX taken out leaves SUAL, giving CASUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a relaxed, unconcerned manner, as in an offhand or casual remark.

clue.text: Tent's top has point

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
an epee is a fencing sword, a weapon fought with the point

explanation.surface: A tent whose roof rises to a sharp peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the conical tent while T plus EPEE builds TEPEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Plains wigwam is a conical tent of poles and skins, so its top comes to a point.

clue.text: Headless dead bird - decomposed, sour-smelling

indicators.note: without a head, the first letter is removed
something decomposed has broken down, so the letters are broken up and reordered

blocks.note: the dodo is the proverbial extinct bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rotting bird carcass gives off a rank, sour stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sour-smelling' looks like a single definition, but the hyphen hides a split: sour is anagram fodder and only 'smelling' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving off a scent or odour, pleasant or not, is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Cyberspace meeting setting up European net to catch the French confrere right out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter for right is dropped from the word before it
setting things up means arranging them, so all the letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
le is French for the
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Organising an online meeting by using a European network to snare a French colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: CONFRERE loses one R to give CONFERE; with E, NET, C and LE that makes fourteen letters to rearrange into TELECONFERENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A discussion held remotely over phone lines or the internet is a meeting conducted in cyberspace.

clue.text: Sleuths are men of insight, playful at heart

indicators.note: something at the heart of another sits inside it, surrounded

blocks.note: seers are prophets, people with visionary insight
arch means mischievously playful, as in an arch smile

explanation.surface: Detectives are perceptive types with a teasing streak underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCH goes into the middle of SEERS: SE-ARCH-ERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives hunt for clues and missing people, so they are those who look for things.

clue.text: Run into East European worker

indicators.note: one thing run into another ends up inside it

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: Bumping into a labourer from Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside POLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for proletarian, the informal word means a member of the labouring working class.

clue.text: First of all, I do love endless relaxation!

definitions.text: First of all, I do love endless relaxation!

indicators.note: the first of every word that follows is taken, one letter from each

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Someone happily admitting that nothing beats a long, unbroken rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole exclamation is what a lazy person who loves doing nothing would say.

clue.text: Fellow expresses hesitation before an escort

indicators.note: coming before means these pieces line up ahead of the last one

blocks.note: a chap is a fellow
er is the sound of hesitating
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: A man hums and haws before asking for a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies and supervises someone, especially a young woman at social events, acting as an escort.

clue.text: Entrails upset? Find the toilets!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A queasy stomach demands a quick dash to the loo.
explanation.definitionFit: Latrines are basic communal toilets, especially in camps or barracks.

clue.text: New leader leaving Lancashire town very quickly

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
a letter leaving a word is taken away from it

blocks.note: the opening letter of this word
Preston is a town in Lancashire, a county in north-west England

explanation.surface: A newly elected party leader rushes out of a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTON drops its N, the first letter of 'New'.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is a musical tempo marking meaning to play fast, and more generally means rapidly or at once.

clue.text: Family is not real, unfortunately

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sad discovery that one's family turns out to be fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by blood or marriage make up a family, and relations is the usual collective word for them.

clue.text: Vegetable contains a mixture of zinc, copper, hydrogen and iodine

indicators.note: a mixture blends ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A health-food label listing the minerals inside a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Zinc is used whole rather than as its symbol Zn, while the other three elements become symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: The zucchini, known in Britain as a courgette, is a small green summer squash eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Baby crab

blocks.note: first meaning: informal British word for a small child
second meaning: a creature that pinches with its claws

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a young crab, but they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for a young child, and also names something that pinches, such as a crab or its claw.

clue.text: Blair ditching British left in favour of PR, that is plain

indicators.note: ditching means throwing away, so these letters leave the name
dropping one thing in favour of another means swapping it for the replacement

blocks.note: Tony Blair, the former British prime minister
B is the abbreviation for British
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written; it stands for public relations
i.e. is the abbreviation for the Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A political jibe that Blair abandoned his British left-wing roots for spin; that much is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: In BLAIR the B and L are replaced by PR, giving PRAIR, then IE is added. 'Plain' looks like part of the jibe but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open area of flat grassland, a plain, especially in North America.

clue.text: Start the game without bruiser on the field

blocks.note: a bully is a thug who throws his weight about
off can mean without, as in off sugar

explanation.surface: The match kicks off with the team's heavy sent off the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A bully-off is the old way of starting a field-hockey game, two players tapping sticks over the ball; a bruiser off the field is literally a bully off.
explanation.definitionFit: In hockey, the bully-off is the face-off that begins play, so the phrase means to start the game.

clue.text: Park most of backside on an upholstered seat

indicators.note: most of a word means one letter of it is missing

blocks.note: a bottom is a backside
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to sit yourself down on a padded chair.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTOM loses its first letter to give OTTOM, followed by AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is a low padded footstool or couch without back or arms, a cushioned seat.

clue.text: Unusual boy rated likely to succeed

blocks.note: odd means unusual
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A peculiar lad tipped for great things.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, an odds-on favourite has a better than even chance of winning.

clue.text: Lyrical disco harp arrangement

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks material, so these letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dance-music version of a harp tune sounds rather poetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic means extravagantly enthusiastic and expressive, like a rhapsody, which is close to lyrical.

clue.text: In reprisal, volley fired in sea-fight

indicators.note: the answer sits in the following words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A naval battle in which one ship fires back in retaliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volley' wants to be the definition, but it supplies the last two letters of the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: A simultaneous discharge of several guns, as from a warship's broadside, is what this word names.

clue.text: Diminutive Egyptian king or teacher

blocks.note: Tut is the familiar short form of Tutankhamun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between a boy pharaoh and a schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive' suggests Tutankhamun was small, but it means his name is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher, or one who teaches a small group at a university.

clue.text: Annual percentage rate? 49? But that's a month!

blocks.note: APR is the standard abbreviation for annual percentage rate
IL is 49 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by a 49 per cent interest rate thinks it must be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The month of April Fools' Day suggests that a 49% rate is a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: April is the fourth month of the year in the Western calendar.

clue.text: Popeye is a normal sort

indicators.note: to sort things is to rearrange them, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that the cartoon hero is just an ordinary guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' reads as a noun meaning type, but here it is a verb telling us to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinach-eating cartoon character is introduced in his theme song as Popeye the Sailor Man.

clue.text: Information-gathering is criminal in late medieval era

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: the Renaissance followed the Middle Ages in Europe
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: A historian's claim that spying on people was a crime in the 1400s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a con, short for convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance is military surveying of enemy territory to collect intelligence, so it is gathering information.
